findings.title: env_drift's claim-hygiene refusal kills 17/17 production mutants pre-capture, a comment-only edit included
findings.claim: With the fork point at the baseline (claim list of 5 scenarios, unchanged by the diff), tests/env_drift.py's claim-hygiene check refuses 17 of 17 production mutants -- including a comment-only edit and a threadpoolctl guard that is equivalent in every supported install -- with INHERITED CLAIMS before any capture, while the unmutated tree passes; tests/mutation_table.py:run_script scores that rc change as 'killed by tests/env_drift.py', and the D3 brief's own pre-screen (env_drift --all <baseline>) inherits the same false kill.
findings.mechanism: check_claims_hygiene() runs before the capture under --all (tests/env_drift.py main, 'if everything:' block). A mutation of integration Python makes claim_kinds() mark the solver claim file as owed; the tree's list equals the base's, so inherited_claims_error() fires. The mutation instrument's drive_spec() passes only ['--all', ref] and never rewrites the claim list for the mutant's diff (what claims-autofix does on a real PR), so the refusal is attributed to the mutant. Affected: every run whose three-dot does not already touch integration Python while the base carries claims -- mutation_table --scope changed on a test-only PR (its documented fallback), the D3 audit pre-screen and the quiet-window GATE_SCOPE=full GOLDEN_MODE=drift re-run of survivors at this baseline. The nightly (--scope full, ref HEAD^1) is NOT affected at this baseline: measured 0/17 refused.

evidence.machine: 4-vCPU cloud Linux container (x86_64, 15 GB), shared with ~13 seats; not the audit box

findings.title: env_drift cache key hashes HPO_* variables no capture reads, so locked or contract-following runs miss the cache
findings.claim: tests/env_drift.py:cache_key over five environments that differ only in the three HPO_* variables the harness contract (HPO_PLANDATA) and tests/run.sh's locked path (run.sh:87-94: HPO_GATE_LOCK_LABEL, HPO_GATE_FLOCK_CHILD=1) set yields 4 distinct keys, while those names are read 0 times by anything a capture executes; each distinct key is a full baseline re-capture (one miss measured at 22m59s wall / 5m54s user at load1~23, provisional).
findings.mechanism: CACHE_ENV_PREFIXES includes 'HPO_' wholesale (tests/env_drift.py:330-334) and _relevant_environment() hashes every matching variable into cache_key_inputs()['environment']. The lock label is per seat and per person, so two locked gate runs of the same commit on one box never share a baseline, and none shares CI's.

evidence.unit: distinct cache keys over 4 capture-equivalent environments (+1 null repeat)
